prompt: Match each attack to who stops it in the shop's design.

pairs.left: A SYN flood against a public IP
Thousands of valid requests to the search page
pairs.right: The WAF's rate limit and caching

prompt: Why can a flood still take down a small application protected only by infrastructure protection?
hint: Whose limits is it tuned to?

choices.text: Infrastructure protection is off by default
choices.why: It is on for every public IP, with nothing to configure.

choices.text: It is tuned to volumes that hurt Azure
choices.why: Right. A flood far below that can still exhaust one shop.

choices.text: It only covers IPv6 addresses
choices.why: It covers public IPs generally.

choices.text: It only protects against layer 7 attacks
choices.why: Layer 7 is the WAF's job; this works at layers 3 and 4.

prompt: What does DDoS Network Protection include that IP Protection does not?

choices.text: Adaptive tuning to your own traffic
choices.why: Both tiers tune to your traffic.

choices.text: Telemetry, alerts and mitigation reports
choices.why: Both tiers provide them.

choices.text: Rapid response and cost protection
choices.why: Right. Those come only with the plan.

choices.text: Protection for layer 7 attacks
choices.why: Neither tier covers layer 7; that is the WAF.

prompt: A DDoS protection plan is linked to virtual ___, and every public IP in them is covered.
hint: The thing a subnet lives in.

prompt: The shop's Front Door has a strict WAF, but the app's azurewebsites.net address answers anybody. What does that mean?

choices.text: Nothing; Front Door still filters every request
choices.why: Requests sent straight to the app never pass through it.

choices.text: Anybody is free to skip the edge
choices.why: Right. The app must accept only Front Door.

choices.text: The WAF automatically extends to the app's address
choices.why: A WAF applies where it is attached, at the edge.

choices.text: DDoS IP Protection covers the gap
choices.why: It does not filter layer 7, and the app's address is not a public IP in a VNet.

prompt: How does App Service know a request really came through the shop's own Front Door?

choices.text: By the client's country
choices.why: Country says nothing about the path.

choices.text: By a password in the URL
choices.why: No such thing; it uses a tag and a header.

choices.text: By the AzureFrontDoor.Backend tag alone
choices.why: Any customer's Front Door uses that tag; the id narrows it.

choices.text: The service tag plus the X-Azure-FDID header
choices.why: Right. The header carries the shop's own Front Door id.

prompt: Put the shop's perimeter layers in order, from the internet inwards.
items: App Service accepting only Front Door
Network security groups in the virtual network
Private endpoints for SQL and Key Vault
trap: Putting the private endpoints first is the slip: they are the centre, with nothing public left to reach.

prompt: At the illustrative prices, 3,000 USD a month for the plan and 200 USD per protected IP, at how many IPs do the two cost the same?
Why does the shop buy neither paid plan today?
hint: Which public IPs would be protected?

choices.text: The plans do not exist in brazilsouth
choices.why: Availability is not the reason given.

choices.text: Front Door makes DDoS attacks impossible
choices.why: It absorbs them at the edge; impossible is not the claim.

choices.text: No customer path uses those IPs
choices.why: Right. Customers enter through Front Door; the condition to revisit is written down.

choices.text: Cost protection already covers any outage
choices.why: Cost protection comes with the plan it is not buying.

prompt: What event would make the shop revisit the decision?
hint: It is written down with the decision.

choices.text: A new month starting
choices.why: The decision depends on the design, not the calendar.

choices.text: A public Application Gateway in brazilsouth
choices.why: Right. Then customers would reach a regional public IP.

choices.text: A rise in WAF blocks
choices.why: That is layer 7, a different layer.

choices.text: The secure score dropping below 80%
choices.why: Posture is a different question.

prompt: Which statements are true of this lesson? Choose all that apply.
hint: Read, not run; arithmetic, not prices.

choices.text: No DDoS plan was created
choices.why: Yes. It needs a subscription.

choices.text: The prices used are illustrative
choices.why: Yes. The price list was out of reach.

choices.text: Layer 7 floods are stopped by DDoS IP Protection
choices.why: No. Layer 7 is the WAF's job.

choices.text: The app must refuse traffic that skipped Front Door
choices.why: Yes. Otherwise the edge is optional.
